clue.text: Highly-rated member of 6 opens county plant

indicators.note: the member and the top grade open up the county, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: a shire is an English county
A is the top grade, so something highly rated is A-rated
MP is a Member of Parliament, and 6 is PARLIAMENT

explanation.surface: A star politician formally opens a county site, perhaps a factory or a botanic garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory being opened, but it is the definition: a coastal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock samphire and marsh samphire are edible coastal plants, also called glasswort.

clue.text: Apparently tolerates soldiers' senselessness

indicators.note: tolerates means puts up, and in this down clue that phrase is taken at face value: the word puts is written upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to tolerate is to put up with, giving puts
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A grumble that the army's apparent tolerance is plain stupidity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tolerates' is 'puts up'; 'Apparently' tells you to read that literally, PUTS written up the grid, giving STUP, then OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state in which one is barely conscious, without one's senses.

clue.text: Maybe gold satisfied nearly everyone

parts.note: to satisfy a need is to meet it, so satisfied is met

indicators.note: nearly means the word for everyone loses its last letter

parts.note: everyone is all

explanation.surface: Perhaps a gold medal pleased almost the whole crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last L of ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is one example of a metal, which 'Maybe' signals.

clue.text: Bear action about new sort of 6

indicators.note: about means the embrace goes round the letter for new

parts.note: a bear hug is the bear's characteristic squeeze

explanation.surface: A bear's behaviour said to be about a new kind of legislature, which makes little sense as a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is PARLIAMENT; a hung one has no party with an overall majority.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislature in which no party holds a majority is described with this word.

clue.text: First of irises in flower on a gorgeous stretch of coastline

indicators.note: in places the first letter of irises inside the flower

parts.note: a crossword flower is something that flows, a river

indicators.note: First of picks the opening letter of irises

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Irises blooming on a lovely stretch of coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the classic crossword river (something that flows), not a bloom; I goes inside RIVER, then A.
explanation.definitionFit: The French and Italian Mediterranean coast is famously beautiful and known by this name.

clue.text: Web designer toured Ipswich, being shown around

indicators.note: around means the displayed letters are turned back to front
being shown means the letters are on display within the words toured Ipswich

explanation.surface: A website designer touring Ipswich, showing the town around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being shown' finds REDIPS in 'touRED IPSwich'; 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arachnid spins a web, so it is a designer of webs in a cryptic sense.

clue.text: Treatment of malaria mostly covered by restricted diet

indicators.note: covered by means the rearranged letters sit inside the word for restricted

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means confined or restricted

indicators.note: treatment works the disease's letters over into a new order
mostly means the last letter of malaria is dropped

explanation.surface: A malaria cure that is mostly a strict diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet' is not food: a Diet is the national assembly of countries such as Japan. 'Treatment of' anagrams MALARI into ARLIAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Diet is the name of national legislative assemblies such as Japan's, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Some members of 6 tell stories about animal clone

parts.note: the DUP, the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, has several MPs at Westminster

indicators.note: about means the fibbing word goes around the animal

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: Politicians spinning tales about a cloned animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A clone is an exact copy, as is a duplicate.

clue.text: Put down for one stopping to tell stories

indicators.note: stopping means the example abbreviation plugs a gap inside the storytelling word

parts.note: to relate is to narrate or tell a story
for one introduces an example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Someone is demoted for halting to spin yarns.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote a team or person to a lower rank or division is to put them down.

clue.text: Fixed 6 up in being prejudiced

indicators.note: in places the turned number inside the word for fixed

parts.note: fixed means set, as in set in stone

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the number is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: here 6 is just the number six, not the cross-reference

explanation.surface: A rigged parliament being biased, read as a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like the cross-reference to 6 down but is just the number; 'up' reads it backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who discriminates against one sex holds a prejudice, so the word describes a prejudiced person.

clue.text: Versatile performer — American — can barely move

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: barely means the word is stripped bare, keeping only its middle letters

explanation.surface: An American performer of many talents who can hardly move.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Ustinov was an actor, writer, director and raconteur, hence versatile. 'barely' strips MOVE to OV.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Ustinov acted, wrote, directed and told stories, a multi-talented entertainer.

clue.text: Law enforcement agency's money cut back

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: the euro is the currency of much of Europe

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A police agency's budget has been cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: The European Union's police cooperation agency is named this, so it is a law enforcement body.

clue.text: Slow dances for members of 6

indicators.note: the letters dance about into a new order

explanation.surface: Slow dances, as at a ball, for MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: A group of owls is called a parliament, so owls are members of 6.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for a group of these birds is a parliament, so each bird is a member.

clue.text: Going back to engineers, 6 protest against government

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the government letter is put beside the protest

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers
here 6 is the Roman numeral VI, not the cross-reference
a sit-in is a protest occupation

explanation.surface: Engineers returning to a protest against the government.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like the cross-reference but is the Roman numeral VI.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit is to go back to a place or topic again.

clue.text: Stutter and tremble painting pupil

indicators.note: to tremble is to shake, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A student artist who stutters and shakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone studying painting at college is a pupil of the fine arts.

clue.text: Essentially, crabby Queen's Speech is out of character

indicators.note: essentially means the essence, the middle letters, of crabby

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; the 's links her to the speech
a rant is a speech, especially a loud one

explanation.surface: A grumpy King's or Queen's Speech that is unlike the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's Speech opens a session of 6, so it feels like a definition, but it is ER + RANT. 'Essentially' takes AB from crabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is aberrant departs from the norm, so it is not typical of someone.

clue.text: Foreign 6's beginning in bilingual German and French is supported by the attorney-general

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in a down entry, supported by means the next piece sits beneath
beginning in picks the first letter of bilingual

parts.note: und is the German for and
est is the French for is
AG is the abbreviation for attorney-general

explanation.surface: A bilingual foreign legislature in German and French, with legal backing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bundestag is the German federal legislature, a parliament abroad.

clue.text: Intended encountered carrying article

indicators.note: carrying means the word for encountered holds the article inside it

parts.note: to have encountered is to have met
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A planned meeting with someone bearing a news item.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meant was planned or intended.

clue.text: 6's official to endorse keeping large staff

indicators.note: keeping means the endorsing word holds the large abbreviation inside

parts.note: to back a plan is to endorse it
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A parliamentary official endorsing a large staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Rod is the House of Lords officer who carries an ebony staff and summons MPs for the State Opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Rod is a senior officer of the House of Lords, the upper chamber at Westminster.

clue.text: With writing materials, left for golf course

parts.note: inks are materials for writing

explanation.surface: Someone abandons pens and paper for a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside golf course on sandy ground is called by this name.

clue.text: Lack of bias not established to perform exhumation

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for established is taken away

parts.note: disinterest means impartiality, a lack of bias
est is the abbreviation for established, as on shopfronts

explanation.surface: An impartial inquiry declines to dig up a body.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume a body is to dig it out of the ground again.

clue.text: 6's business club submerged in river

indicators.note: submerged in means the club sits inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a bat is a club used in games

explanation.surface: A club's business dumped into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a British river, flowing through Chester, and another in Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: Discussion of motions is the main activity of a legislature.

clue.text: Spooner's academics go for Foot

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of the two words are swapped, as Rev Spooner did

parts.note: dons are university academics
to go, colloquially, is to relieve oneself, to pee

explanation.surface: Academics taking a stroll on foot, read as a whimsical instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: Hear DONS PEE as 'don spee' and swap the opening sounds D and SP.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of two stressed syllables has this name in poetry.

clue.text: Pig eats old member of Irish 6 as a snack

indicators.note: eats means the pig takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a hog is a pig
TD is Teachta Dala, a member of the Dail, the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A pig devours an elderly Irish politician as a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A TD (Teachta Dala) is a member of the Dail, the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage in a bun is a quick street snack.

clue.text: Quebec and, initially, Ontario have organised satisfactory means of payment

indicators.note: organised means these letters are arranged into a new order
initially takes the first letters of Ontario and have

parts.note: OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: Two Canadian provinces have set up an acceptable payment system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives O and H, joined to QUEBEC and 'organised' to make CHEQUEBO, then OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of cheques is used to pay bills, so it is a way of paying.

clue.text: Card game very much over

parts.note: far means very much, as in far better
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over, a set of six balls

explanation.surface: A card game that is very much finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is an old gambling game played with cards against a banker.

clue.text: Sound car gets round

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A car comes round in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as healthy; it is the noun for recorded sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded or transmitted sound is called this, as in an audio track.

clue.text: Book products of 6

definitions.meaning: the fifth book of the New Testament, about the Apostles
laws passed by a legislature are called by this name

explanation.surface: A book about the output of the legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible book about the apostles is so named, and statutes passed by parliament share the name.

clue.text: Withdraw army unit about to be buried in rubbish

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a unit of the British Army

indicators.note: buried in means the word for about goes inside the rubbish

parts.note: tat is shoddy goods, rubbish
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An army unit is ordered to pull back, about to be buried under junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies that withdraw from a position are said to fall back.

clue.text: Interpreted legal document describes fake

indicators.note: describes in its literal sense of drawing round: the document goes round the fake

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
cod means fake or mock, as in cod Latin

explanation.surface: A legal document is read as describing a forgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' is used in the geometric sense of drawing a line around.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decoded has had its hidden meaning worked out.

clue.text: Policeman meets unpleasant person with small fingers?

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
git is British slang for a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A police officer meets a nasty character with tiny fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'git' is mild British slang for an unpleasant person. The question mark marks fingers as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingers are examples of the body's digits, along with toes.

clue.text: More eggs scrambled by member of 6

indicators.note: scrambled, like eggs, means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An MP demands extra scrambled eggs, perhaps at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Rees-Mogg is a Conservative politician, long an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob of that surname was a Conservative MP for North East Somerset.
